question: In table tennis, how many consecutive serves does each player get before switching?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under the standard laws of **Table Tennis** established by the **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF)**, the right to serve alternates between opponents after every **2 points** scored.
 
• The sequence of service remains constant throughout the game regardless of which player wins the point, ensuring each player receives an equal number of opportunities to initiate play.
 
• This rotation continues until the game ends or until the score reaches **10-10**, at which point the game enters a phase known as a **Deuce**.
 
• In a **standard match**, a game is won by the first player or pair to score **11 points**, provided there is a margin of at least **2 points** over the opponent.
 
• The **server** must strike the ball so that it first touches their court and then touches the receiver's court directly, passing over or around the **net assembly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Service Exceptions and Variations**:

 
 
• **Deuce Scenarios**: When the score is tied at **10-10**, the sequence of serving and receiving remains the same, but each player shall serve for only **1 point** in turn until a lead of **2 points** is established.
 
• **Expedite System**: If a game is not finished after **10 minutes** of play (unless both players have scored at least 9 points), the **Expedite System** is implemented. Under this rule, service alternates after every **single point**.
 
• **Doubles Play**: The service rotation involves four players. The server first serves to the receiver, then the receiver becomes the server, and the partner of the initial server becomes the new receiver.
 
• **Service Technique**: The ball must be placed on the **open palm** of the stationary free hand and thrown at least **16 cm** into the air without imparting spin before being struck.
